$comment:
chess.jsonc — Chess game logic in json-fn

All chess rules (move generation, check detection, checkmate/stalemate)
expressed entirely as JSON function definitions.

Board: flat 64-element array, index = rank*8 + file.
rank 0 = row 1 (white's back rank), file 0 = a-file.
Index 0 = a1, 7 = h1, 8 = a2, ..., 63 = h8.

Pieces: single characters.
Uppercase = white: P N B R Q K
Lowercase = black: p n b r q k
null = empty square.

Game state: { board: [...64], turn: "w"|"b", status: "playing"|"checkmate"|"stalemate" }

Scope: all piece movement, captures, check, checkmate, stalemate, pawn
double-move, and auto-promotion to queen. No castling, en passant, or
draw rules.

makePiece.$comment: makePiece(color, type) → uppercase if "w", lowercase if "b"

slideDir.$comment:
=========================================================================
Layer 2 — Pseudo-Legal Move Generation
=========================================================================
slideDir(board, row, col, dr, dc, color) → [targetIdx...]
Recursive: walk one direction collecting valid target squares.
Stops on board edge, own piece (exclusive), or enemy piece (inclusive).

slideMoves.$comment:
slideMoves(board, idx, color, dirs) → [targetIdx...]
Calls slideDir for each direction, flattens results.

steppingMoves.$comment:
steppingMoves(board, idx, color, offsets) → [targetIdx...]
Non-sliding pieces (knight, king): each offset is a single candidate step,
kept when in bounds and not blocked by a friendly piece.

pawnMoves.$comment:
pawnMoves(board, idx, color) → [targetIdx...]
Forward 1, forward 2 from start rank, diagonal captures.

captures.$comment: Diagonal captures via flatMap over [-1, 1] column offsets

pieceMoves.$comment:
pieceMoves(board, idx) → [targetIdx...]
Dispatches to the appropriate move generator based on piece type.

slideCheck.$comment:
=========================================================================
Layer 3 — Check Detection

Uses the "look from the target square" strategy: from the square in
question, look outward in all attack patterns to find enemy pieces.
=========================================================================
slideCheck(board, row, col, dr, dc) → piece | null
Walk one direction and return the first piece found, or null.

isAttacked.$comment:
isAttacked(board, idx, byColor) → boolean
Is the square at idx attacked by any piece of byColor?

pawnSrcRow.$comment: Pawn attacks: white pawns attack from row-1, black from row+1

findKing.$comment: findKing(board, color) → index of king, or -1

applyMove.$comment:
=========================================================================
Layer 4 — Legal Moves and Game Status
=========================================================================
applyMove(board, from, to) → new board
Moves the piece, clears the source, handles auto-promotion to queen.

isLegalMove.$comment:
isLegalMove(board, from, to, turn) → boolean
Validates ownership, pseudo-legality, and that the king is not left in check.

hasAnyLegalMove.$comment:
hasAnyLegalMove(board, color) → boolean
Checks whether the side to move has at least one legal move.

playMove.$comment:
=========================================================================
Layer 5 — Top-Level Entry Point
=========================================================================
playMove(state, from, to) → new state
Validates the game is still active and the move is legal.
Returns the updated state on success, or the original state unchanged.

newGame.$comment:
=========================================================================
Layer 6 — CLI, Parsing, and Display

Everything below here exists so the host program can be a thin shell
that only handles process I/O (argv in, stdout/stderr out, state file
persistence). All parsing, rendering, and user-facing messaging lives
in json-fn.
=========================================================================
newGame() → initial game state.

parseSquare.$comment:
parseSquare("e2") → 12, or null if invalid.
Uses indexOf on the file/rank alphabets in lieu of charCodeAt.

parseMove.$comment: parseMove("e2e4") or parseMove("e2 e4") → { "from": 12, "to": 28 }, or null.

pieceGlyph.$comment: pieceGlyph(piece) → unicode chess symbol, or "·" for null.

formatBoard.$comment: formatBoard(board) → multi-line rendered board with file labels.

$fn: a  b  c  d  e  f  g  h

statusLine.$comment:
statusLine(state) → "  White to move", "  White to move  [CHECK]",
"  Checkmate — Black wins!", "  Stalemate — draw!".

boardSection.$comment:
boardSection(state, header) → "
[header]

[board]

[status]
"
header is an optional first line above the board ("" to omit).

showResult.$comment: showResult(state) → command result for the "show" subcommand.

resetResult.$comment:
resetResult() → command result for "reset". Tells the host to delete
the state file; the next invocation will load newGame() afresh.

$return.output:
Chess — json-fn edition

  Usage:  bun run typescript/examples/chess.ts <command>

  Commands:
    e2e4 / e2 e4    Make a move (algebraic notation)
    show             Display the current board (default)
    reset            Start a new game
    help             Show this message

moveResult.$comment:
moveResult(state, argv) → command result for any move-shaped argv.
Validates parse, game-active, and legality; returns the appropriate
result object for each failure mode or the post-move board for success.
The "illegal move" check that used to live in the host is folded in
here via an explicit isLegalMove call.

legal.$comment: Legality (only consulted when move parses and game is active).

$fn: ". Use algebraic notation like 'e2e4' or 'e2 e4'.
). Run 'reset' to start a new game.

handleCommand.$comment:
handleCommand(state, argv) → unified command result object:
{ output: string, stderr: string, newState: state|null,
reset: bool, exitCode: number }
The host's only job is to read state, call this, then act on the
returned fields (write/delete state file, print, exit).
